ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, water is conveyed from storage tank A into closed tank B using centrifugal pump $P_{1}$ with an efficiency of 75%. It is known that the characteristic curve equation of pump $P_{1}$ is: $$H=40-0.006q_v^2$$ where $H$ is the head (m), and $q_v$ is the flow rate ($\mathrm{m^3/h}$). The maximum conveying capacity of this system is $50\mathrm{m^3/h}$, and the pipe dimensions are all 108mm×4mm. Assume that all flows are in the fully turbulent region; the distances between the outlet valves of the two pumps and the centrifugal pump outlets, and the distances between the outlet valves and the confluence point, are very short, and the resistance of the suction pipeline can be neglected. Find the system resistance when single pump $P_{1}$ operates under the maximum flow condition (expressed in m liquid column).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is storage tank A, marked with a pressure of 0.1 MPa (gauge pressure), and its liquid level line 0—0′ has a height of 5 m relative to the bottom reference height; the right side is closed tank B, marked with a pressure of 0.2 MPa (gauge pressure). In the figure, the liquid level line 2—2′ of B is 10 m higher than the middle pipeline 1—1′, while 1—1′ is 2 m higher than the bottom reference, so the liquid level height of B is 12 m. From the figure, the height difference of the liquid level of B relative to the liquid level of A is 12 - 5 = 7 m. Reasoning calculation: Under the maximum flow condition, q_v = 50 m^3/h. The characteristic curve of pump P1 is H = 40 - 0.006q_v^2, therefore H_P1 = 40 - 0.006 × 50^2 = 25 m. The static pressure head difference from A to B is (0.2 - 0.1) MPa / (ρg) = 100000 / 9810 ≈ 10.2 m water column. The static head is the pressure head difference plus the elevation difference, namely 10.2 + 7 = 17.2 m. The head provided by the single pump at this maximum flow rate is used to overcome the static head and the system resistance, therefore the system resistance h_f = 25 - 17.2 = 7.8 m liquid column.

raw_record.question_text:
As shown in the figure, water is conveyed from storage tank A into closed tank B using centrifugal pump $P_{1}$ with an efficiency of 75%. It is known that the characteristic curve equation of pump $P_{1}$ is:

$$H=40-0.006q_v^2$$

where $H$ is the head (m), and $q_v$ is the flow rate ($\mathrm{m^3/h}$). The maximum conveying capacity of this system is $50\mathrm{m^3/h}$, and the pipe dimensions are all 108mm×4mm. Assume that all flows are in the fully turbulent region; the distances between the outlet valves of the two pumps and the centrifugal pump outlets, and the distances between the outlet valves and the confluence point, are very short, and the resistance of the suction pipeline can be neglected. Find the system resistance when single pump $P_{1}$ operates under the maximum flow condition (expressed in m liquid column).

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: identify A and B as closed vessels, read their gauge pressures and the elevations of their free surfaces. From the text take the maximum flow q_v = 50 m^3/h and the P1 characteristic H = 40 - 0.006q_v^2. Evaluate the pump head at q_v = 50: H_P1 = 40 - 0.006(50)^2 = 25 m. Compute the static head from A to B as pressure head difference plus elevation difference: about 10.2 + 7 = 17.2 m. The required system resistance at this flow is then h_f = H_P1 - 17.2 ≈ 7.8 m liquid column.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, water is conveyed from storage tank A into closed tank B using centrifugal pump $P_{1}$ with an efficiency of 75%. It is known that the characteristic curve equation of pump $P_{1}$ is: $$H=40-0.006q_v^2$$ where $H$ is the head (m), and $q_v$ is the flow rate ($\mathrm{m^3/h}$). The maximum conveying capacity of this system is $50\mathrm{m^3/h}$, and the pipe dimensions are all 108mm×4mm. Assume that all flows are in the fully turbulent region; the distances between the outlet valves of the two pumps and the centrifugal pump outlets, and the distances between the outlet valves and the confluence point, are very short, and the resistance of the suction pipeline can be neglected. Find the system resistance when single pump $P_{1}$ operates under the maximum flow condition (expressed in m liquid column).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is storage tank A, marked with a pressure of 0.1 MPa (gauge pressure), and its liquid level line 0—0′ has a height of 5 m relative to the bottom reference height; the right side is closed tank B, marked with a pressure of 0.2 MPa (gauge pressure). In the figure, the liquid level line 2—2′ of B is 10 m higher than the middle pipeline 1—1′, while 1—1′ is 2 m higher than the bottom reference, so the liquid level height of B is 12 m. From the figure, the height difference of the liquid level of B relative to the liquid level of A is 12 - 5 = 7 m. Reasoning calculation: Under the maximum flow condition, q_v = 50 m^3/h. The characteristic curve of pump P1 is H = 40 - 0.006q_v^2, therefore H_P1 = 40 - 0.006 × 50^2 = 25 m. The static pressure head difference from A to B is (0.2 - 0.1) MPa / (ρg) = 100000 / 9810 ≈ 10.2 m water column. The static head is the pressure head difference plus the elevation difference, namely 10.2 + 7 = 17.2 m. The head provided by the single pump at this maximum flow rate is used to overcome the static head and the system resistance, therefore the system resistance h_f = 25 - 17.2 = 7.8 m liquid column.
